title.raw: 卷一百四十三 志5: 禮志下 Volume 143: Treatises 5 Rites 2

sentences.zh: 禮志下

translations.literal: Treatise on Rites, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Rites, Part Two

sentences.zh: 後唐長興元年九月，太常禮院奏：「來年四月孟夏，禘饗於太廟。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Changxing of Later Tang, the Court of Imperial Rites of the Ministry of Rites memorialized: "In the fourth month of next year, at the first month of summer, a di sacrifice and communal feast shall be held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of the Changxing era of Later Tang, the Court of Imperial Rites submitted a memorial: "Next year, in the fourth month—the first month of summer—a di sacrifice and communal offering are to be held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple."

sentences.zh: 謹按禮經，三年一祫以孟冬，五年一禘以孟夏。

translations.literal: According to the ritual canon, there is one xia sacrifice every three years in early winter, and one di sacrifice every five years in early summer.
translations.idiomatic: As the ritual classics prescribe, a collective xia sacrifice is held every three years in early winter, and a di sacrifice every five years in early summer.

sentences.zh: 已毀未毀之主，並合食於太祖之廟，逐廟功臣，配饗於太廟之庭。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets both already removed and not yet removed shall all partake together in the shrine of the Grand Ancestor, and meritorious ministers of each shrine shall receive associated offerings in the court of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets whether already removed from their shrines or not shall all share a communal meal at the Grand Ancestor's shrine, while meritorious ministers from each shrine shall receive associated offerings in the temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 本朝寶應元年定禮，奉景皇帝為始封之祖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying of this dynasty the rites were fixed, honoring Emperor Jing as the ancestor of the original enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were codified in the first year of the Baoying era, this dynasty honored Emperor Jing as the founder of the original enfeoffment line.

sentences.zh: 既廟號太祖，百代不遷，每遇禘祫，位居東向之尊，自代祖元皇帝、高祖、太宗已下，列聖子孫，各序昭穆南北相向，合食於前。

translations.literal: Once his temple title was Grand Ancestor, he was never to be removed for a hundred generations; at each di and xia sacrifice he held the honored seat facing east. From the Yuan Emperor, the founding ancestor of Dai, and the High Ancestor and the Grand Ancestor Taizong downward, the successive sage emperors and their descendants were each arranged in zhao and mu order facing north and south, and all partook together before him.
translations.idiomatic: Once enshrined as the Grand Ancestor, he was never to be displaced for a hundred generations; at every di and xia sacrifice he took the seat of honor facing east. From the Yuan Emperor, the High Ancestor, and Grand Ancestor Taizong down through their descendants, each generation was arranged in zhao and mu order facing north and south, and all shared the communal meal before him.

sentences.zh: 聖朝中興，重修宗廟，今太廟見饗高祖、太宗、懿宗、昭宗、獻祖、太祖、莊宗七廟，太祖景皇帝在祧廟之數，不列廟饗。

translations.literal: When the sacred dynasty was restored, the ancestral temples were rebuilt. At present the Imperial Ancestral Temple offers sacrifices to seven shrines: the High Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor, Emperor Yi, Emperor Zhao, the Founding Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor (Zhuangzong), and seven temples in all; the Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing counts among the distant-ancestor shrines and is not listed among the temples receiving regular offerings.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty's restoration the ancestral temples were rebuilt. The Imperial Ancestral Temple now maintains seven shrines with regular offerings: to the High Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor, Emperor Yi, Emperor Zhao, the Founding Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor, and Emperor Zhuangzong. Emperor Jing, titled Grand Ancestor, is counted among the distant-ancestor shrines and is not included in the regular temple offerings.

sentences.zh: 將來禘禮，若奉高祖居東向之尊，則禘饗不及於太祖、代祖；

translations.literal: At the coming di ceremony, if the High Ancestor is placed in the seat of honor facing east, then the di offering will not reach the Grand Ancestor and the Dai founding ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: At the next di ceremony, if the High Ancestor is given the seat of honor facing east, the di offering will not include the Grand Ancestor and the Dai founding ancestor;

sentences.zh: 若以祧廟太祖居東向之位，則又違於禮意。

translations.literal: if the Grand Ancestor of the distant-ancestor shrine is placed in the seat facing east, that again violates the intent of the rites.
translations.idiomatic: yet if the Grand Ancestor in the distant-ancestor shrine is placed in the eastern seat of honor, that would again violate ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 今所司修奉祧廟神主，及諸色法物已備，合預請參詳，事須具狀申奏。

translations.literal: The departments concerned have now prepared the spirit tablets for the distant-ancestor shrine and all ritual implements of every kind; they should be consulted in advance, and the matter must be reported in a formal memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices have now prepared the spirit tablets for the distant-ancestor shrine and all requisite ritual implements; the matter should be reviewed in advance and reported in a formal memorial.

sentences.zh: 」敕下尚書省集百官詳議。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued to the Department of State Affairs to assemble all officials for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the Department of State Affairs to convene all officials for full deliberation.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書韓彥惲等奏議曰：「伏以本朝尊受命之祖景皇帝為始封之君，百代不遷，長居廟食，自貞觀至於天祐，無所改更，聖祖神孫，左昭右穆。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Han Yanbing and others submitted a deliberative memorial, saying: "We note that this dynasty honors Emperor Jing, the ancestor who received the Mandate, as the lord of the original enfeoffment, never to be removed for a hundred generations, long receiving temple offerings; from the Zhenguan era to the Tianyou era nothing was changed, with sacred ancestors and divine descendants arranged zhao on the left and mu on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Han Yanbing and others submitted their opinion: "This dynasty honors Emperor Jing, the ancestor who received the Mandate, as the founder of the enfeoffment line—never displaced for a hundred generations and always receiving temple offerings. From the Zhenguan era through Tianyou the arrangement was never altered, with sacred forebears and their descendants set out zhao on the left and mu on the right.

sentences.zh: 自中興國祚，再議宗祊，以太祖景皇帝在祧廟之數，不列祖宗，欲尊太祖之位，將行東向之儀，爰命群臣，同議可否。

translations.literal: Since the restoration of the imperial fortune, the ancestral temples have been debated anew; because the Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing counts among the distant-ancestor shrines and is not listed among the ancestors, wishing to honor the Grand Ancestor's position, the eastern-facing rite will be performed; the emperor has charged the ministers to deliberate together whether this is permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's restoration the ancestral shrines have been reconsidered. Because Emperor Jing, titled Grand Ancestor, is counted among the distant-ancestor shrines and excluded from the main ancestral line, the court wishes to honor his position by performing the eastern-facing rite and has ordered the ministers to deliberate whether this is proper.

sentences.zh: 伏詳本朝列聖之舊典，明皇定禮之新規，開元十年，特立九廟，子孫遵守，歷代無虧。

translations.literal: We have examined in detail the old statutes of the successive sage emperors of this dynasty and the new regulations for fixing the rites under Emperor Ming; in the tenth year of Kaiyuan nine temples were specially established, and descendants have observed this without loss through successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Upon examining this dynasty's established precedents for successive emperors and the new ritual regulations promulgated under Emperor Ming, we find that in the tenth year of Kaiyuan nine ancestral temples were specially established; descendants have upheld this arrangement through every subsequent reign without impairment.

sentences.zh: 今既行定禮之規，又以祧太祖之室。

translations.literal: Now the fixed ritual regulations are already in force, yet the Grand Ancestor's shrine is also placed among the distant ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The court now follows the codified ritual regulations while also relegating the Grand Ancestor's shrine to the distant-ancestor line.

sentences.zh: 昔德宗朝，將行禘祫之禮，顏真卿議請奉獻祖居東向之位，景皇帝暫居昭穆之列，考之於貞元，則以為誤，行之於今日，正得其禮。

translations.literal: In the Dezong era, when di and xia sacrifices were to be performed, Yan Zhenqing proposed that the Founding Ancestor be placed in the seat facing east and Emperor Jing temporarily placed in the zhao-mu array; examined against the Zhenyuan practice, that was held to be an error, but carried out today it accords with the rites.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Dezong's reign, as di and xia sacrifices were being planned, Yan Zhenqing proposed placing the Founding Ancestor in the eastern seat of honor and Emperor Jing temporarily in the zhao-mu arrangement. Judged against Zhenyuan practice that was deemed an error, yet applied today it would be ritually correct.

sentences.zh: 今欲請每遇禘祫之歲，暫奉景皇帝居東向之尊，自元皇帝以下，敘列昭穆。

translations.literal: We now request that in every year when di and xia are performed, Emperor Jing be temporarily placed in the seat of honor facing east, and from the Yuan Emperor downward the zhao-mu order be arranged.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore propose that at each di and xia sacrifice Emperor Jing be temporarily given the eastern seat of honor, with the Yuan Emperor and all below arranged in zhao-mu order.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 周廣順三年冬十月，禮儀使奏：「郊廟祝文，禮例云：古者文字皆書於冊，而有長短之差。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "For prayer texts at suburban and temple sacrifices, ritual precedent states: in antiquity all writing was inscribed on bound documents, which differed in length.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the third year of the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, the Commissioner of Ritual submitted a memorial: "Regarding prayer texts for suburban and temple sacrifices, ritual precedent holds that in antiquity all texts were written on bound documents, which varied in length.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉郊廟祝文書於冊。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin, suburban and temple prayer texts were written on bound documents.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei and Jin dynasties, suburban and temple prayer texts were written on bound documents.

sentences.zh: 唐初悉用祝版，唯陵廟用玉冊，玄皇親祭郊廟，用玉為冊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang all used prayer boards; only imperial tombs and temples used jade books, and when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade was used for the books.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang dynasty prayer boards alone were used, except at imperial tombs and temples where jade books were employed; when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade books were used.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，博士陸淳議，準禮用祝版，祭已燔之，可其議。

translations.literal: In the Dezong era, Academician Lu Chun proposed, in accordance with the rites, to use prayer boards and burn them after the sacrifice; his proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: During Dezong's reign Academician Lu Chun proposed using prayer boards in accordance with the rites and burning them once the sacrifice was complete; his proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年親祭，又用竹冊，當司準《開元禮》，並用祝版。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan, when the emperor sacrificed in person, bamboo books were again used; the responsible office, following the Kaiyuan Rites, used prayer boards throughout.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan the emperor sacrificed in person and bamboo books were used again, but the responsible office, following the Kaiyuan Rites, employed prayer boards throughout.

sentences.zh: 梁朝依禮行之，至明宗郊天，又用竹冊。

translations.literal: The Liang dynasty followed the rites in practice; by the time of Emperor Mingzong's suburban sacrifice to Heaven, bamboo books were again used.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang dynasty followed the rites in practice; by Emperor Mingzong's suburban sacrifice to Heaven, bamboo books had come back into use.

sentences.zh: 今詳酌禮例，允以祝版為宜。

translations.literal: Having now examined ritual precedent in detail, it is appropriate to use prayer boards.
translations.idiomatic: Having now reviewed ritual precedent in detail, prayer boards are the appropriate choice.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 周廣順三年九月，南郊，禮儀使奏：「郊祀所用珪璧制度，準禮，祀上帝以蒼璧；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, at the southern suburban sacrifice, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "The regulations for gui and bi disks used in suburban sacrifice, according to the rites: to sacrifice to the Supreme Lord use the dark-green bi;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year of Guangshun of Later Zhou, at the southern suburban sacrifice, the Commissioner of Ritual submitted a memorial: "The specifications for gui and bi disks used in suburban sacrifice follow the rites: the Supreme Lord is worshipped with a dark-green bi;

sentences.zh: 祀地祇以黃琮；

translations.literal: to sacrifice to the earthly spirits use the yellow cong;
translations.idiomatic: the earthly spirits with a yellow cong;

sentences.zh: 祀五帝以珪璋琥璜琮，其玉各依本方正色，祀日月以珪璋，祀神州以兩珪有邸。

translations.literal: to sacrifice to the Five Emperors use gui, zhang, hu, huang, and cong; each jade follows its native direction and proper color; to sacrifice to the sun and moon use gui and zhang; to sacrifice to the sacred land within the realm use two gui with base.
translations.idiomatic: the Five Emperors with gui, zhang, hu, huang, and cong, each jade in the color of its cardinal direction; the sun and moon with gui and zhang; and the sacred land within the realm with a pair of gui with base.

sentences.zh: 其用幣，天以蒼色，地以黃色，配帝以白色，日月五帝各從本方之色，皆長一丈八尺。

translations.literal: For the silks used, heaven is dark in color, earth yellow, the associated emperors white; the sun, moon, and Five Emperors each follow the color of their direction; all are one zhang and eight chi in length.
translations.idiomatic: The silks used are dark for heaven, yellow for earth, and white for the associated emperors; the sun, moon, and Five Emperors each take the color of their direction; all are one zhang and eight chi long.

sentences.zh: 其珪璧之狀，譬圓而琮八方，珪上銳而下方，半珪曰璋，琥為虎形，半璧曰璜，其珪璧琮璜皆長一尺二寸四。

translations.literal: The forms of the gui and bi: the bi is round and the cong eight-sided; the gui is pointed above and square below; half a gui is called zhang; hu is in the shape of a tiger; half a bi is called huang; the gui, bi, cong, and huang are each one chi, two cun, and four fen in length.
translations.idiomatic: In form the bi is round and the cong octagonal; the gui tapers to a point above and is square below; half a gui is a zhang; hu is shaped like a tiger; half a bi is a huang; each gui, bi, cong, and huang measures one chi, two cun, and four fen.

sentences.zh: 珪有邸，邸，本也，珪著於璧而整肅也。

translations.literal: A gui may have a base; di means root—the gui is set upon the bi and thereby made whole and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: A gui may have a base; di means "root"—the gui is mounted on the bi and thereby made whole and dignified.

sentences.zh: 日月星辰以珪璧五寸，前件珪璧雖有圖樣，而長短之說或殊。

translations.literal: For the sun, moon, and stars, gui and bi of five cun are used; although the foregoing gui and bi have illustrated forms, accounts of their length sometimes differ.
translations.idiomatic: For the sun, moon, and stars, gui and bi of five cun are used; though the foregoing gui and bi have illustrated forms, accounts of their dimensions sometimes differ.

sentences.zh: 按唐開元中，玄宗詔曰：「祀神以玉，取其精潔，比來用瑉，不可行也。

translations.literal: According to the Kaiyuan era of Tang, an edict of Emperor Xuanzong stated: "To worship the spirits with jade is to take its purity and refinement; recently min jade has been used, which cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Kaiyuan period of Tang, Emperor Xuanzong's edict stated: "Spirits are worshipped with jade for its purity and refinement; of late inferior min jade has been used, which is not acceptable.

sentences.zh: 如或以玉難辦，寧小其制度，以取其真。

translations.literal: If jade is difficult to obtain, it is better to reduce the scale of the regulations so as to secure authenticity.
translations.idiomatic: If genuine jade is hard to obtain, it is better to scale down the specifications than sacrifice authenticity.

sentences.zh: 』今郊廟所修珪璧，量玉大小，不必皆從古制，伏請下所司修制。

translations.literal: ' The gui and bi now prepared for suburban and temple sacrifice should be sized according to the jade available and need not all follow the ancient regulations; we respectfully request that the responsible offices be ordered to manufacture them.
translations.idiomatic: ' The gui and bi now being prepared for suburban and temple sacrifice should be sized to the jade available and need not all follow ancient specifications; we respectfully request that the responsible offices be directed to manufacture them.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年夏四月，禮官博士等準詔，議祭器、祭玉制度以聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the fourth year of Xiande, ritual officials and academicians, in accordance with an edict, deliberated on the regulations for sacrificial vessels and sacrificial jade and reported their findings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the fourth year of Xiande, ritual officials and academicians, acting on imperial command, deliberated on regulations for sacrificial vessels and sacrificial jade and reported their conclusions.

sentences.zh: 時國子祭酒尹拙引崔靈恩《三禮義宗》云：「蒼璧所以祀天，其長十有二寸，蓋法天之十二時。

translations.literal: At that time Guozi Libationer Yin Zhuo cited Cui Lingen's Three Rites Meaning and Tradition, saying: "The dark bi is used to worship Heaven; its length is twelve cun, taking the twelve hours of Heaven as its model.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guozi Libationer Yin Zhuo cited Cui Lingen's Three Rites Meaning and Tradition: "The dark bi worships Heaven; it is twelve cun long, modeling Heaven's twelve hours.

sentences.zh: 」又引《江都集》、《白虎通》等諸書所說，云：「璧皆外圓內方。

translations.literal: " He also cited the Jiangdu Collection, the Baihu Tong, and other books, saying: "All bi are round outside and square inside.
translations.idiomatic: " He also cited the Jiangdu Collection, the Baihu Tong, and other works stating that "all bi are round outside and square inside."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「璜琮所以祀地，其長十寸，以法地之數。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The huang and cong are used to worship Earth; they are ten cun long, taking Earth's number as their model.
translations.idiomatic: " He further stated: "The huang and cong worship Earth; they are ten cun long, modeling Earth's number.

sentences.zh: 其琮外方內圓，八角而有好。

translations.literal: The cong is square outside and round inside, eight-sided, with a perforation.
translations.idiomatic: The cong is square outside, round inside, octagonal, with a perforation.

sentences.zh: 」國子博士聶從義以為璧內外皆圓，其徑九寸。

translations.literal: " Guozi Academician Nie Congyi held that the bi is round both inside and outside, with a diameter of nine cun.
translations.idiomatic: " Guozi Academician Nie Congyi held that the bi is round inside and out, with a diameter of nine cun.

sentences.zh: 又按阮氏、鄭玄圖皆云九寸，《周禮·玉人》職又有九寸之璧。

translations.literal: He also examined the diagrams of the Ruan clan and Zheng Xuan, which all say nine cun; the Office of Jade Workers in the Zhou Rites also specifies a bi of nine cun.
translations.idiomatic: He also consulted the diagrams of the Ruan school and Zheng Xuan, all of which specify nine cun, and the Office of Jade Workers in the Zhou Rites likewise describes a nine-cun bi.

sentences.zh: 及引《爾雅》云：「肉倍好謂之璧，好倍肉謂之瑗，肉好若一謂之環。

translations.literal: He cited the Erya: "When the rim is twice the perforation it is called a bi; when the perforation is twice the rim it is called a yuan; when rim and perforation are equal it is called a ring.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Erya: "When the rim is twice the hole it is a bi; when the hole is twice the rim it is a yuan; when rim and hole are equal it is a ring.

sentences.zh: 」郭璞註云：「好，孔也；

translations.literal: " Guo Pu annotated: "Hao means the hole;
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Pu annotated: "Hao means the hole;

sentences.zh: 肉，邊也。

translations.literal: rou means the rim.
translations.idiomatic: rou means the rim."

sentences.zh: 」而不載尺寸之數。

translations.literal: " But it does not record dimensions.
translations.idiomatic: " But it records no dimensions.

sentences.zh: 崇義又引《冬官·玉人》云「璧好三寸」，《爾雅》云「肉倍好謂之璧」，兩邊肉各三寸，通好共九寸，則其璧九寸明矣。

translations.literal: Chongyi also cited the Winter Office Jade Workers: "the perforation of the bi is three cun," and the Erya: "when the rim is twice the perforation it is called a bi"; each rim three cun, with the perforation totaling nine cun, then the bi of nine cun is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi also cited the Winter Office's Jade Workers: "the bi's perforation is three cun," and the Erya: "when the rim is twice the perforation it is a bi"; with three cun on each side of the rim and the hole totaling nine cun, the nine-cun bi is clearly established.

sentences.zh: 崇義又云：「璜琮八方以象地，每角各剡出一寸六分，共長八寸，厚一寸。

translations.literal: Chongyi also said: "The huang and cong are eight-sided to represent Earth; from each corner one cun and six fen are cut away, totaling eight cun in length and one cun in thickness.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi also said: "The huang and cong are octagonal to represent Earth; one cun and six fen are cut from each corner, for a total length of eight cun and thickness of one cun.

sentences.zh: 按《周禮疏》及阮氏圖並無好。

translations.literal: According to the Zhou Rites commentary and the Ruan diagrams, there is no perforation.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Zhou Rites commentary and the Ruan diagrams, there is no perforation.

sentences.zh: 」又引《冬官·玉人》云：「琮八角而無好。

translations.literal: " He also cited the Winter Office Jade Workers: "the cong is eight-sided and without a perforation.
translations.idiomatic: " He also cited the Winter Office Jade Workers: "the cong is octagonal and without a perforation.

sentences.zh: 」崇義又云：「琮璜珪璧，俱是祀天地之器，而《爾雅》唯言璧環瑗三者有好，其餘黃琮諸器，並不言之，則璜琮八角而無好明矣。

translations.literal: " Chongyi also said: "The cong, huang, gui, and bi are all vessels for worshipping Heaven and Earth, yet the Erya speaks only of the bi, ring, and yuan as having perforations; the remaining yellow cong and other vessels are not mentioned—thus it is clear that the huang and cong are eight-sided and without perforation.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongyi also argued: "The cong, huang, gui, and bi all worship Heaven and Earth, yet the Erya mentions perforations only for the bi, ring, and yuan; the yellow cong and other vessels are not discussed—so the huang and cong are clearly octagonal and without perforation.

sentences.zh: 」太常卿田敏以下議，以為尹拙所說雖有所據，而崇義援《周禮》正文，其理稍優，請從之。

translations.literal: " Director of the Court of Imperial Rites Tian Min and others deliberated and held that although Yin Zhuo's account had some basis, Chongyi's citation of the authoritative text of the Zhou Rites was somewhat superior in reasoning; they requested approval of his view.
translations.idiomatic: " Director of the Court of Imperial Rites Tian Min and others found that while Yin Zhuo's account had some support, Chongyi's appeal to the authoritative Zhou Rites text was the stronger argument; they recommended adopting his view.

sentences.zh: 其諸祭器制度，亦多以崇義所議為定。

translations.literal: For the regulations governing other sacrificial vessels as well, Chongyi's deliberations were largely adopted as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for other sacrificial vessels likewise largely followed Chongyi's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年秋八月，兵部尚書張昭上言：「今月十二日，伏蒙宸慈召對，面奉聖旨，每年祀祭，多用太牢，念其耕稼之勞，更備犧牲之用，比諸豢養，特可湣傷，令臣等討故事，可以佗牲代否。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn in the second year of Xiande, Minister of War Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial: "On the twelfth day of this month I was graciously summoned for an audience and received the imperial command in person: at the annual sacrifices too many tai-lao offerings are used; mindful of the labor of plowing and sowing, and of the further provision of sacrificial animals, compared with ordinary rearing this is especially pitiable; the emperor ordered us to investigate precedent and determine whether other victims may be substituted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in the second year of Xiande, Minister of War Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial: "On the twelfth of this month I was summoned to audience and received the imperial command in person: our annual sacrifices use too many tai-lao offerings; mindful of the labor of farming and the cost of raising sacrificial stock—far more burdensome than ordinary husbandry—the emperor ordered us to search precedent and determine whether other victims might be substituted.

sentences.zh: 臣仰稟綸言，退尋禮籍，其三牲八簋之制，五禮六樂之文，著在典彜，叠相沿襲，累經朝代，無所改更。

translations.literal: I received the imperial words, withdrew, and searched the ritual records: the regulations for the three victims and eight gui dishes, the texts of the five rites and six music, are set down in the canonical codes and handed down through successive reigns without change through many dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: I received the imperial charge, withdrew, and examined the ritual records: the regulations for three victims and eight gui, the texts of the five rites and six music, are recorded in the canonical codes and handed down through dynasty after dynasty without alteration.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古者燔黍捭豚，尚多質略，近則梁武面牲竹脯，不可宗師，雖好生之德則然，於奉先之儀太劣。

translations.literal: I have heard that in antiquity roasted millet and split suckling pig were offered, still largely plain and simple; recently Liang Wudi used face-meat and bamboo jerky, which cannot serve as a model for the ancestral rites—though the virtue of sparing life is understandable, the rites for honoring ancestors are far too deficient.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that in antiquity roasted millet and split suckling pig were offered in a largely plain and simple manner; more recently Emperor Wu of Liang used face-meat and bamboo jerky, which cannot serve as a model for ancestral rites—though compassion for living creatures is admirable, the rites for honoring ancestors become far too meager.

sentences.zh: 蓋禮主於信，孝本因心，黍稷非馨，鬼神饗德，不必牲牢之巨細，籩豆之方圓，茍血祀長保於宗祧，而牲俎何須於繭栗。

translations.literal: Rites rest on sincerity, filial piety springs from the heart; millet and grain are not fragrant—the spirits feast on virtue; the size of victims and the roundness or squareness of platters need not matter; so long as blood sacrifice long preserves the ancestral temples, why must the sacrificial meat be as large as silkworm cocoons?
translations.idiomatic: Rites rest on sincerity and filial piety on the heart; millet and grain are not fragrant in themselves—the spirits feast on virtue. Victims need not be large nor platters perfectly formed; so long as blood sacrifice preserves the ancestral line, why must the offering be as grand as silkworm cocoons?

sentences.zh: 但以國之大事，儒者久行，易以佗牢，恐未為便。

translations.literal: Yet because these are great affairs of state long practiced by the literati, to replace them with other victims may not be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because these are great affairs of state long upheld by the literati, substituting other victims may prove impractical.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚見，其南北郊、宗廟社稷、朝日夕月等大祠，如皇帝親行事，備三牲；

translations.literal: In my humble view, for great sacrifices such as the southern and northern suburbs, the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, the morning sun and evening moon, if the emperor performs the rite in person, the three victims should be provided;
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, for major sacrifices—the southern and northern suburbs, the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, the morning sun and evening moon—when the emperor performs the rite in person the three victims should be provided;

sentences.zh: 如有司攝行事，則用少牢已下。

translations.literal: if a responsible official performs the rite by proxy, then shao-lao or less may be used.
translations.idiomatic: when an official performs the rite by proxy, shao-lao or lesser offerings may suffice.

sentences.zh: 雖非舊典，貴減牲牛。

translations.literal: Although this is not the old canon, it is valuable for reducing oxen offered in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Though not the old canon, this would significantly reduce oxen sacrificed.

sentences.zh: 」是時太常卿田敏又奏云：

translations.literal: " At that time Director Tian Min also memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Director Tian Min also submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣奉聖旨為祠祭用犢事。

translations.literal: Your subject has received the imperial command regarding sacrificial calves.
translations.idiomatic: I have received the imperial command regarding sacrificial calves.

sentences.zh: 今太僕寺供犢，一年四季都用犢二十二頭。

translations.literal: At present the Court of the Imperial Stud provides calves; all four seasons together use twenty-two calves.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Stud currently supplies calves; all four seasons together require twenty-two head.

sentences.zh: 《唐會要》武德九年十月詔：「祭祀之意，本以為民，窮民事神，有乖正直，殺牛不如礿祭，明德即是馨香，望古推今，民神一揆。

translations.literal: The Tang Huiyao records an edict of the tenth month of the ninth year of Wude: "The intent of sacrifice is fundamentally for the people; to impoverish the people to serve the spirits violates uprightness; killing oxen is not as good as a frugal sacrifice; clear virtue is itself fragrance; surveying antiquity and the present, the people and the spirits are one in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Huiyao records an edict from the tenth month of the ninth year of Wude: "Sacrifice exists fundamentally for the people's sake; impoverishing the people to serve the spirits violates righteousness; a frugal sacrifice is better than slaughtering oxen; clear virtue is itself fragrance; surveying past and present, people and spirits share one standard.

sentences.zh: 其祭圜丘、方澤、宗廟已外，並可止用少牢，用少牢者用特牲代。

translations.literal: Apart from sacrifices at the Round Mound, the Square Mound, and the ancestral temple, all may use only shao-lao; where shao-lao is used, a single victim may substitute.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the Round Mound, Square Mound, and ancestral temple, all sacrifices may use only shao-lao; where shao-lao is used, a single victim may substitute.

sentences.zh: 時和年豐，然後克修常禮。

translations.literal: In years of peace and abundance the regular rites may then be fully observed.
translations.idiomatic: Only in years of peace and abundance may the full regular rites be observed.

sentences.zh: 」又按《會要》天寶六載正月十三日赦文：「祭祀之典，犧牲所備，將有達於虔誠，蓋不資於廣殺。

translations.literal: " He also examined the Huiyao: an amnesty of the thirteenth day of the first month of the sixth year of Tianbao stated: "In the canon of sacrifice, victims are provided so that reverence may reach sincerity; lavish slaughter is not required.

sentences.zh: 自今後每大祭祀，應用骍犢，宜令所司量減其數，仍永為恒式。

translations.literal: Henceforth at each great sacrifice, where crimson calves are used, the responsible offices should reduce the number according to measure and make this a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth at each great sacrifice requiring crimson calves, the responsible offices shall reduce the number by measure and establish this as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 其年起請以舊料每年用犢二百一十二頭，今請減一百七十三頭，止用三十九頭，余祠饗並停用犢。

translations.literal: The annual requisition had been two hundred and twelve calves by old quota; it is now requested to reduce by one hundred and seventy-three head, using only thirty-nine; for remaining sacrifices and feasts calves are discontinued entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The annual requisition had stood at two hundred and twelve calves; it is now proposed to reduce by one hundred and seventy-three, retaining only thirty-nine; all remaining sacrifices and feasts shall discontinue calves entirely.

sentences.zh: 」至上元二年九月二十一日赦文：「國之大事，郊祀為先，貴其至誠，不美多品。

translations.literal: " An amnesty of the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the second year of Shangyuan stated: "Among great affairs of state, suburban sacrifice comes first; what is valued is utmost sincerity, not abundance of offerings.
translations.idiomatic: " An amnesty of the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the second year of Shangyuan stated: "Among great affairs of state suburban sacrifice comes first; utmost sincerity is valued, not abundance of offerings.

sentences.zh: 黍稷雖設，猶或非馨；

translations.literal: Though millet and grain are set out, they may still lack fragrance;
translations.idiomatic: Though millet and grain are set out, they may lack true fragrance;

sentences.zh: 牲牢空多，未為能饗。

translations.literal: victims may be plentiful yet still fail to satisfy the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: victims may be plentiful yet still fail to satisfy the spirits.

sentences.zh: 圜丘、方澤，任依恒式，宗廟諸祠，臨時獻熟，用懷明德之馨，庶合西鄰之祭。

translations.literal: For the Round Mound and Square Mound, follow the regular form; for ancestral temple and other sacrifices, offer cooked meat at the time of sacrifice, using the fragrance of clear virtue, in accord with the sacrifice of the western neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: For the Round Mound and Square Mound follow the regular form; for the ancestral temple and other sacrifices offer cooked meat at the time of sacrifice, using the fragrance of clear virtue in the manner of the western neighbor's offering.

sentences.zh: 其年起請昊天上帝、太廟各太牢一，余祭並隨事市供。

translations.literal: The annual requisition for the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the Grand Temple each uses one tai-lao; remaining sacrifices are supplied by market purchase as the occasion requires.
translations.idiomatic: The annual requisition provides one tai-lao each for the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the Grand Temple; all remaining sacrifices are supplied by market purchase as occasion requires.

sentences.zh: 」若據天寶六載，自二百一十二頭減用三十九頭；

translations.literal: According to the sixth year of Tianbao, from two hundred and twelve head the use was reduced to thirty-nine;
translations.idiomatic: Under the sixth year of Tianbao, use was cut from two hundred and twelve head to thirty-nine;

sentences.zh: 據武德九年，每年用犢十頭，圜丘四，方澤一，宗廟五；

translations.literal: according to the ninth year of Wude, ten calves were used annually—four for the Round Mound, one for the Square Mound, five for the ancestral temple;
translations.idiomatic: under the ninth year of Wude, ten calves were used annually—four for the Round Mound, one for the Square Mound, five for the ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 據上元二年起請只昊天上帝、太廟，又無方澤，則九頭矣。

translations.literal: according to the Shangyuan second-year requisition only the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the Grand Temple, with no Square Mound, then nine head.
translations.idiomatic: under the Shangyuan second-year requisition only the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the Grand Temple—with no Square Mound—nine head sufficed.

sentences.zh: 今國家用牛，比開元、天寶則不多，比武德、上元則過其大半。

translations.literal: The present dynasty's use of oxen is not greater than under Kaiyuan and Tianbao, but exceeds Wude and Shangyuan by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: This dynasty's use of oxen is not greater than under Kaiyuan and Tianbao, yet exceeds Wude and Shangyuan by well over half.

sentences.zh: 案《會要》，太僕寺有牧監，掌孳課之事。

translations.literal: According to the Huiyao, the Court of the Imperial Stud has pasture supervisors who oversee breeding and taxation affairs.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Huiyao, the Court of the Imperial Stud maintains pasture supervisors overseeing breeding and taxation.

sentences.zh: 乞今後太僕寺養孳課牛，其犢遇祭昊天前三月養之滌宮，取其蕩滌清潔，余祭則不養滌宮。

translations.literal: We request that henceforth the Court of the Imperial Stud raise breeding stock; calves for sacrifice to the Supreme Lord three months before the rite are raised in the purification palace to secure cleansing and purity; for other sacrifices the purification palace is not used.
translations.idiomatic: We request that henceforth the Court raise breeding stock; calves for the Supreme Lord's sacrifice are raised three months beforehand in the purification palace to ensure cleansing and purity; other sacrifices need not use the purification palace.

sentences.zh: 若臨時買牛，恐非典故。

translations.literal: If oxen are purchased at the last moment, we fear this is not according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Purchasing oxen at the last moment, we fear, would violate precedent.

sentences.zh: 奉敕：「祭祀尚誠，祝史貴信，非誠與信，何以事神！

translations.literal: Edict: "Sacrifice values sincerity; prayer-officers value trustworthiness—without sincerity and trustworthiness, how may one serve the spirits!
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edict: "Sacrifice values sincerity; prayer-officers value trustworthiness—without sincerity and trustworthiness, how may one serve the spirits!

sentences.zh: 礿祭重於殺牛，黍稷輕於明德，犧牲之數，具載典經。

translations.literal: A frugal sacrifice is weightier than killing oxen; millet and grain are lighter than clear virtue; the numbers of victims are fully set forth in the canonical codes.
translations.idiomatic: A frugal sacrifice outweighs slaughtering oxen; millet and grain weigh less than clear virtue; victim numbers are fully set forth in the canonical codes.

sentences.zh: 前代以來，或有增損，宜采酌中之禮，且從貴少之文。

translations.literal: Through former ages there have sometimes been increases and reductions; the moderate rites should be adopted, and for the present the principle of valuing fewer offerings should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages sometimes increased or reduced offerings; the moderate rites should be adopted, and for now the principle of fewer offerings should prevail.

sentences.zh: 起今後祭圜丘、方澤、社稷，並依舊用犢；

translations.literal: Henceforth sacrifices at the Round Mound, Square Mound, and altars of soil and grain shall continue to use calves as before;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth sacrifices at the Round Mound, Square Mound, and altars of soil and grain shall continue to use calves as before;

sentences.zh: 其太廟及諸祠，宜準上元二年九月二十一日制，並不用犢。

translations.literal: for the Grand Temple and other sacrifices, follow the regulation of the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the second year of Shangyuan and discontinue calves entirely.
translations.idiomatic: for the Grand Temple and other sacrifices follow the regulation of the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the second year of Shangyuan and discontinue calves entirely.

translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performs the rite in person, follow the regular form."

sentences.zh: 後唐同光二年三月十日，祠部奏：「本朝舊儀，太微宮每年五存獻，其南郊壇每年四祠祭。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the third month of the second year of Tongguang of Later Tang, the Department of Sacrifices memorialized: "According to this dynasty's established practice, the Supreme Palace of the Great Ultimate receives five seasonal offerings each year, and the southern suburban altar four sacrificial rites annually.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the third month of the second year of Tongguang of Later Tang, the Department of Sacrifices submitted a memorial: "By this dynasty's established practice, the Supreme Palace of the Great Ultimate receives five seasonal offerings yearly, and the southern suburban altar four sacrifices annually.

sentences.zh: 吏部申奏，請差中書門下攝太尉行事，其太廟及諸郊壇，並吏部差三品已上攝太尉行事。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel memorialized requesting that the Secretariat and Chancellery act as Grand Master of Ceremonies by proxy; for the Grand Temple and other suburban altars, officials of the third rank and above from the Ministry of Personnel shall act as Grand Master of Ceremonies by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel requested that the Secretariat and Chancellery serve as acting Grand Master of Ceremonies; for the Grand Temple and other suburban altars, officials of third rank and above from the Ministry of Personnel shall serve in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 至其年七月，中書門下奏：「據尚書祠部狀，每年太微宮五薦獻，南郊壇四祠祭，並宰相攝太尉行事，惟太廟時祭，獨遣庶僚，雖為舊規，慮成闕禮。

translations.literal: By the seventh month of that year the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "According to the memorial of the Ministry of Rites' Department of Sacrifices, each year the Supreme Palace receives five offerings and the southern suburban altar four sacrifices, all performed by the chief ministers acting as Grand Master of Ceremonies; only for seasonal offerings at the Grand Temple are lesser officials dispatched—though this is old practice, we fear it constitutes a breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month of that year the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted a memorial: "According to the Department of Sacrifices, each year the Supreme Palace receives five offerings and the southern suburban altar four sacrifices, all with chief ministers acting as Grand Master of Ceremonies; only seasonal offerings at the Grand Temple are assigned to lesser officials—though longstanding practice, we fear this falls short of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，今後太廟祠祭，亦望差宰臣行事。

translations.literal: We have deliberated and request that henceforth sacrifices at the Grand Temple also be assigned to chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: We have deliberated and request that henceforth Grand Temple sacrifices also be performed by chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，禮儀使奏：「伏準禮經，喪三年不祭，惟祭天地社稷為越紼行事，此古制也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "According to the ritual canon, during the three-year mourning period no sacrifices are performed except for Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain, which are conducted by passing the mourning cord—this is the ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, the Commissioner of Ritual submitted a memorial: "The ritual canon holds that during the three-year mourning period no sacrifices are performed except to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain, conducted by passing the mourning cord over the ritual garb—this is the ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 爰自漢文，益尊神器，務徇公絕私之義，行以日易月之作制，事久相沿，禮從順變。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wen of Han, the sacred vessels were increasingly honored; public duty was pursued and private feeling set aside; the regulation of replacing months with days was enacted; the practice has long continued and the rites have yielded to convenience.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wen of Han onward the sacred vessels grew ever more honored; public duty was pursued and private feeling set aside; the regulation replacing months with days was enacted; the practice has long continued and ritual has yielded to convenience.

sentences.zh: 今園陵已畢，祥練既除，宗廟不可以乏享，神祇不可以廢祀，宜遵禮意，式展孝思。

translations.literal: Now the imperial tombs are complete and the mourning and lesser mourning periods concluded; the ancestral temple cannot lack offerings, nor the spirits be left without sacrifice; the intent of the rites should be followed and filial devotion displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial tombs are complete and the mourning periods concluded; the ancestral temple cannot lack offerings, nor the spirits be left unserved; ritual intent should be followed and filial devotion displayed.

sentences.zh: 伏請自貞簡太后升祔禮畢，應宗廟伎樂及群祀，並準舊施行。

translations.literal: We respectfully request that after the enshrinement rites for Empress Dowager Zhenjian are complete, temple music and all group sacrifices resume according to former practice.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully request that once the enshrinement rites for Empress Dowager Zhenjian are complete, temple music and all collective sacrifices resume according to former practice.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 天成四年九月，太常寺奏：「伏見大祠則差宰臣行事，中祠則差諸寺卿監行事，小祠則委太祝、奉禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Tiancheng, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: "We note that for great sacrifices chief ministers are assigned to perform the rite, for medium sacrifices directors of the various courts are assigned, and for minor sacrifices the invoker and ceremonial officer are entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Tiancheng, the Court of Imperial Rites submitted a memorial: "For great sacrifices chief ministers perform the rite; for medium sacrifices directors of the various courts; for minor sacrifices the invoker and ceremonial officer.

sentences.zh: 今後凡小祠，請差五品官行事。

translations.literal: Henceforth for all minor sacrifices, we request that officials of the fifth rank perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth we request that officials of the fifth rank perform all minor sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，中書門下奏：「太微宮、太廟、南郊壇，宰臣行事宿齋，百官皆預人事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "For the Supreme Palace of the Great Ultimate, the Grand Temple, and the southern suburban altar, when chief ministers perform the rite they observe fasting quarters; all officials participate in the arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted a memorial: "At the Supreme Palace of the Great Ultimate, the Grand Temple, and the southern suburban altar, chief ministers performing the rite observe fasting quarters, and all officials participate in the arrangements.

sentences.zh: 伏以奉命行事，精誠齋宿，儻遍見於朝官，涉虔於祠祭。

translations.literal: We note that receiving the command to perform the rite requires sincere fasting; if the entire body of court officials is seen there, this may impair the reverence of the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the command to perform the rite requires sincere fasting; if the entire court is present, reverence for the sacrifice may be compromised.

translations.literal: Henceforth when chief ministers perform the rite, we request that neither the civil nor the military cohort be permitted at the fasting quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth when chief ministers perform the rite, neither the civil nor the military cohort should be admitted to the fasting quarters.

translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Secretariat and Chancellery requested that while chief ministers observe fasting within the palace they not attend court formation, affix seals, or the dawn audience.

translations.idiomatic: On national mourning days, officials under oath of abstinence for a sacrifice shall not attend incense offerings, nor shall capital cases be reported for imperial decision.

translations.idiomatic: During fasting for great sacrifices, banquets should not be held.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.idiomatic: Henceforth we request that on days of great or medium sacrifice the imperial carriage not go abroad.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，太常博士路航奏：「比來小祠已上，公卿皆著祭服行事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, Academician of the Court of Imperial Rites Lu Hang memorialized: "Recently for minor sacrifices and above, public ministers all wear sacrificial robes when performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, Court of Imperial Rites Academician Lu Hang submitted a memorial: "Of late, for minor sacrifices and above, public ministers have worn sacrificial robes when performing the rite.

sentences.zh: 近日唯郊廟、太微宮具祭服，五郊迎氣、日月諸祠，並只常服行事，兼本司執事人等，皆著隨事衣裝，狼藉鞋履，便隨公卿升降於壇墠。

translations.literal: Recently only at suburban altars and the Supreme Palace are sacrificial robes provided; for the five suburban altars welcoming the seasons, the sun and moon, and other sacrifices, all wear only ordinary dress when performing the rite; moreover the responsible personnel of this office all wear clothing suited to the occasion, with sloppy shoes, and ascend and descend the altar mounds alongside the public ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Recently only suburban altars and the Supreme Palace provide sacrificial robes; for the five seasonal suburban altars, the sun and moon, and other sacrifices all wear ordinary dress, while responsible personnel wear whatever is at hand, in sloppy footwear, and ascend the altar mounds alongside the ministers.

sentences.zh: 按祠部令，中祠以上，應齋郎等升壇行事者，並給潔服，事畢收納。

translations.literal: According to the regulations of the Department of Sacrifices, for medium sacrifices and above, sacrificial attendants and others who ascend the altar to perform the rite should all be issued clean garments, to be collected after the affair is concluded.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Department of Sacrifices regulations, for medium sacrifices and above all attendants who ascend the altar should receive clean garments, collected afterward.

sentences.zh: 今後中祠已上，公卿請具祭服，執事升壇人並著履，具緋衣幘子。

translations.literal: Henceforth for medium sacrifices and above, public ministers should be provided sacrificial robes; those ascending the altar should wear shoes, with scarlet garments and caps.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth for medium sacrifices and above ministers should wear sacrificial robes; those ascending the altar should wear proper shoes, scarlet garments, and caps.

sentences.zh: 又，臣檢《禮閣新儀》，太微宮使卯時行事。

translations.literal: Moreover, your subject has examined the New Rites of the Ritual Archive: the Supreme Palace rite is performed at the mao hour.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the New Rites of the Ritual Archive specifies that the Supreme Palace rite is performed at the mao hour.

sentences.zh: 近年依諸郊廟例，五更初便行事，今後請依舊以卯時。

translations.literal: In recent years, following the precedent of suburban altars and temples, the rite has been performed at the beginning of the fifth watch; henceforth we request following the old practice at the mao hour.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, following suburban and temple precedent, the rite has been performed at the fifth watch; henceforth we request restoring the mao hour.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年五月，中書門下奏：「據太常禮院申，明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝今月二十日祔廟，太尉合差宰臣攝行。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "According to the memorial of the Court of Imperial Rites, Emperor Mingzong, the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial, is to be enshrined in the temple on the twentieth day of this month; the Grand Master of Ceremonies should be assigned to a chief minister by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai, the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: "The Court of Imperial Rites states that Emperor Mingzong, the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial, is to be enshrined on the twentieth of this month; a chief minister should serve as acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 緣馮道在假；

translations.literal: Feng Dao is on leave;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao is on leave;

sentences.zh: 李愚十八日私忌，在致齋內；

translations.literal: Li Yu's private mourning day falls on the eighteenth, within the fasting period;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu's private mourning anniversary falls on the eighteenth, within the fasting period;

sentences.zh: 今劉昭又奏見判三司事煩，請免祀事。

translations.literal: now Liu Xu has also memorialized that he is burdened with adjudicating the Three Departments and requests exemption from the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu has memorialized that he is occupied adjudicating the Three Departments and requests exemption from the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今與禮官參酌，諸私忌日，遇大朝會，入閣宣召，尚赴朝參。

translations.literal: Having deliberated with the ritual officials: on private mourning days, when a great court assembly or summons to the inner court occurs, attendance at court is still required.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation with ritual officials: on private mourning days, when a great court assembly or summons to the inner court occurs, attendance is still required.

sentences.zh: 今祔饗事大，忌日屬私，齋日請比大朝會宣召例，差李愚行事。

translations.literal: The enshrinement affair is greater; the mourning day is a private matter; for the fasting day we request applying the precedent of attendance at a great court assembly or summons—Li Yu should be assigned to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Enshrinement is a greater affair and the mourning day a private one; for the fasting day we request the precedent of attendance at court summons—Li Yu should perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 晉開運三年六月，西京留司監祭使奏：「以祠祭所定行事官，臨日或遇疾病，或奉詔赴闕，留司吏部郎中一人主判，有闕便依次第定名，庶無闕事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Kaiyun of Jin, the western capital's acting commissioner for supervising sacrifices memorialized: "When the official assigned to perform a sacrifice on a given day encounters illness or is summoned to court by edict, the Ministry of Personnel's director in the western capital presides; if there is a vacancy the next name in order is assigned, so that no sacrifice lacks an officiant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Kaiyun of Jin, the western capital's acting sacrifice commissioner reported: "When the assigned officiant falls ill or is summoned to court, the western capital's Ministry of Personnel director presides; vacancies are filled in order so no sacrifice lacks an officiant.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 《永樂大典》卷一萬七千五十二。

translations.literal: Yongle Encyclopedia, juan 17052.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle Encyclopedia, juan 17052.

sentences.zh: 天成三年十一月，太常定唐少帝為昭宣光烈考皇帝，廟號景宗。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Tiancheng, the Court of Imperial Rites fixed for the Tang Lesser Emperor the posthumous title Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor, with temple name Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Tiancheng, the Court of Imperial Rites assigned the Tang Lesser Emperor the posthumous title Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor, with temple name Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 博士呂朋龜奏：「謹按禮經，臣不誄君，稱天以謚之，是以本朝故事，命太尉率百僚奉謚冊告天於圜丘，回讀於靈座前，並在七月之內，謚冊入陵。

translations.literal: Academician Lü Penggui memorialized: "According to the ritual canon, subjects do not bestow posthumous titles on their lord; Heaven is invoked to confer the title—therefore by this dynasty's established practice the Grand Master of Ceremonies leads the hundred officials in presenting the title document and reporting to Heaven at the Round Mound; returning, it is read before the spirit seat, all within the seventh month, and the title document enters the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Lü Penggui submitted a memorial: "The ritual canon holds that subjects do not bestow posthumous titles on their lord; Heaven is invoked to confer the title. By established practice the Grand Master of Ceremonies leads the hundred officials in presenting the title document to Heaven at the Round Mound; returning, it is read before the spirit seat, all within the seventh month, and the document enters the tomb.

sentences.zh: 若追尊定謚，命太尉讀謚冊於太廟，藏冊於本廟。

translations.literal: If posthumous honor and a fixed title are conferred, the Grand Master of Ceremonies reads the title document at the Grand Temple and the document is stored in that temple.
translations.idiomatic: When posthumous honor and a fixed title are conferred retroactively, the Grand Master of Ceremonies reads the title document at the Grand Temple and the document is stored there.

sentences.zh: 伏以景宗皇帝，頃負沈冤，歲月深遠，園陵已修，不祔於廟，則景宗皇帝親在七廟之外。

translations.literal: We note that Emperor Jing long bore a deep injustice; the years are distant and the imperial tombs have been restored; if he is not enshrined in the temple, then Emperor Jing personally stands outside the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing long bore a deep injustice; years have passed and his tombs are restored—if he is not enshrined in the temple, he remains outside the seven shrines.

sentences.zh: 今聖朝申冤，追尊定謚，重新帝號，須撰禮儀。

translations.literal: Now the sacred court redresses the injustice, conferring posthumous honor and a fixed title and renewing the imperial designation; ritual procedures must be drafted.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court redresses this injustice, conferring posthumous honor, a fixed title, and a renewed imperial designation; ritual procedures must be drafted.

sentences.zh: 又，《禮》云：君不逾年不入宗廟。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Rites state: a lord does not enter the ancestral temple within a year of death.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Rites state that a lord does not enter the ancestral temple within a year of death.

sentences.zh: 且漢之殤、沖、質，君臣已成，晉之惠、懷、湣，俱負艱難，皆不列高食，止祀於園寢。

translations.literal: Moreover, Han's Shang, Chong, and Zhi; Jin's Hui, Huai, and Min—all bore hardship; none received lofty offerings in the temple, being worshipped only at the tomb palace.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Shang, Chong, and Zhi; Jin's Hui, Huai, and Min—all bore hardship; none received lofty temple offerings, being worshipped only at the tomb palace.

sentences.zh: 臣等切詳故實，欲請立景宗皇帝廟於園所，命使奉冊書寶綬，上謚於廟，便奉太牢祀之，其四時委守奉薦。

translations.literal: Your subjects have examined former practice in detail and request establishing a temple to Emperor Jing at the tomb precinct; envoys shall present the document, seal, and cord; the posthumous title shall be proclaimed at the temple and a tai-lao offered; the four seasons shall be entrusted to guardians for regular offerings.
translations.idiomatic: We have examined precedent and request establishing a temple to Emperor Jing at the tomb precinct; envoys shall present the document, seal, and cord, proclaim the posthumous title, and offer tai-lao; guardians shall maintain seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 請下尚書省集三省官詳議施行。

translations.literal: We request that the Department of State Affairs convene officials of the three departments for detailed deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: We request that the Department of State Affairs convene the three departments for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 」右散騎常侍蕭希甫等議請依禮院所奏。

translations.literal: " Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Xiao Xifu and others deliberated and requested following the Court of Imperial Rites' memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xifu and others recommended following the Court of Imperial Rites' proposal.

sentences.zh: 奉敕：宜令本州城內選地起廟。

translations.literal: Edict: A site within the prefectural city should be selected to erect a temple.
translations.idiomatic: Edict: A site within the prefectural city should be selected for the temple.

sentences.zh: 乃於曹州立廟。

translations.literal: A temple was then established in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was then established in Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，中書門下奏：「先據太常寺定少帝謚昭宣光烈孝皇帝，號景宗者。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "Previously the Court of Imperial Rites fixed the Lesser Emperor's posthumous title as Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor, with the designation Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year, the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: "The Court of Imperial Rites had assigned the Lesser Emperor the posthumous title Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor, with temple name Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 伏以景宗生曾為帝，饗乃承祧，既號景宗，合入宗廟，如不入宗廟，難以言宗。

translations.literal: We note that Emperor Jing in life was once emperor; in sacrifice he continues the ancestral line—once titled Emperor Jing, he should enter the ancestral temple; if he does not enter the temple, it is difficult to speak of him as an ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing in life was once emperor and in sacrifice continues the ancestral line—once titled Emperor Jing he should enter the ancestral temple; without temple enshrinement he cannot properly be called an ancestor.

sentences.zh: 於理而論，祧一遠廟，安少帝神主於太廟，即昭穆序而宗祀正。

translations.literal: In principle, removing one distant shrine and placing the Lesser Emperor's spirit tablet in the Grand Temple would set zhao-mu order and make ancestral worship correct.
translations.idiomatic: In principle, removing one distant shrine and placing the Lesser Emperor's tablet in the Grand Temple would restore zhao-mu order and correct ancestral worship.

sentences.zh: 今或且居別廟，即請不言景宗，但雲昭宣光烈孝皇帝。

translations.literal: If for now he dwells in a separate temple, we request not speaking of Emperor Jing but only of the Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: If he remains in a separate temple for now, we request omitting the temple name Emperor Jing and referring only to the Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 兼冊文內有『基』字，是玄宗廟諱，雖尋常詔敕皆不回避，少帝是繼世之孫，不欲斥列聖之諱，今改『基』為『宗』字。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the title document is the character ji, a taboo of Emperor Xuanzong's temple name; though ordinary edicts need not avoid it, the Lesser Emperor is a successor grandson and we do not wish to violate the taboo of successive sage emperors; we now change ji to zong.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the title document contains the character ji, taboo of Emperor Xuanzong's temple name; though ordinary edicts need not avoid taboo, the Lesser Emperor is a successor grandson and we do not wish to violate successive emperors' taboos; ji is therefore changed to zong.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

translations.idiomatic: (Editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：《風俗通》陳孔璋云：尊卑有敘，喪祭哀敬，各有攸終，欲令言著而可遵，事施而不犯。

translations.literal: (Five Dynasties Essentials: Fengsu Tong—Chen Kongzhang states: High and low have order; mourning sacrifices and reverence each have their proper end, wishing to make words established and followable and affairs carried out without violation.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Five Dynasties Essentials, citing the Fengsu Tong: Chen Kongzhang writes that high and low have their order; mourning, sacrifice, and reverence each have their proper end, so that words may be established for observance and affairs carried out without violation.

sentences.zh: 《禮》云：「卒哭之後，宰執木鐸徇於宮，曰舍故而諱新。

translations.literal: The Rites state: "After the end of wailing, the minister bearing a wooden clapper announces through the palace: set aside the old taboo and observe the new.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state: "After the end of wailing, the minister bearing a wooden clapper announces through the palace: set aside the old taboo and observe the new."

sentences.zh: 」故，謂毀廟之主也，恩遠屬絕，名不可諱。

translations.literal: " Gu means the lord of a destroyed shrine; when kinship is distant and the line severed, the name may not be tabooed.
translations.idiomatic: " Gu refers to the lord of a destroyed shrine; when kinship is distant and the line severed, the name need not be tabooed.

sentences.zh: 今昭宣上去玄宗十四世，奏改冊文，非典故也。）〉

translations.literal: The Illustrious Emperor is fourteen generations below Emperor Xuanzong; to memorialize changing the title document is not according to precedent.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious Emperor stands fourteen generations below Emperor Xuanzong; memorializing a change to the title document violates precedent.)〉

sentences.zh: 八月戊申，明宗服兗冕，禦文明殿，追冊昭宣光烈孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On the day wushen of the eighth month, Emperor Mingzong wore the yuan crown and robe and presided at the Hall of Civilizing Brilliance to confer the title document on the Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day of the eighth month, Emperor Mingzong wore the yuan crown and robe and presided at the Hall of Civilizing Brilliance to confer the title on the Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，冊使兵部尚書盧質押冊出應天門登車，鹵簿鼓吹前導，入都亭驛，翌日，登車赴曹州。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded, Title Document Envoy Minister of War Lu Zhi escorted the document out through the Gate of Responding to Heaven, mounted his carriage with guards of honor and musicians leading, entered the Capital Pavilion relay station, and the next day mounted his carriage for Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites concluded, Title Document Envoy Minister of War Lu Zhi escorted the document through the Gate of Responding to Heaven, mounted his carriage with guards and musicians, entered the Capital Pavilion relay station, and departed for Cao Prefecture the next day.

sentences.zh: 時議者以追尊則可，立之為宗，不入太廟，深為失禮。

translations.literal: Contemporaries held that posthumous honor was permissible, but establishing him as an ancestor without entering the Grand Temple was a deep breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held posthumous honor permissible, but establishing him as an ancestor without Grand Temple enshrinement was a grave breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 夫言宗者，功業纂於祖禰，德澤被於生民，發號申令可也。

translations.literal: To speak of an ancestor is to gather achievement upon forebears and ancestors, with virtue extending to the living people, so that commands may be issued and orders proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor gathers achievement upon forebears, with virtue extending to the people, so that commands may be issued and orders proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 且輝王纂嗣之日，國命出於賊臣，君父銜冤，母後塗炭，遭罹放逐，鼎祚覆亡，追謚易名，當循故實。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the day when Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, the nation's mandate issued from treacherous ministers; the lord and father bore injustice, the queen mother suffered ruin, they met exile and banishment, and the imperial fortune was overthrown; to confer a posthumous title and change the name should follow established practice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui succeeded, the nation's mandate issued from treacherous ministers; lord and father bore injustice, the queen mother suffered ruin, exile followed, and the dynasty fell—posthumous titles should follow established practice.

sentences.zh: 如漢之沖、質，晉之閔、懷，但尊稱而無廟號；

translations.literal: Such as Han's Chong and Zhi, Jin's Min and Huai—only honored titles without temple names;
translations.idiomatic: Han's Chong and Zhi, Jin's Min and Huai received only honored titles without temple names;

sentences.zh: 前代亡國者周赧、漢獻、魏陳留，亦不稱宗；

translations.literal: former ages' fallen states—Zhou's Nan, Han's Xian, Wei's Chenliu—also were not called ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: fallen states of former ages—Zhou's Nan, Han's Xian, Wei's Chenliu—were likewise not called ancestors;

sentences.zh: 中興之追謚者孺子嬰，光武竟無追宗之典。

translations.literal: those posthumously honored at restoration—Infant Ying, yet Guangwu ultimately had no precedent of posthumous ancestor designation.
translations.idiomatic: those posthumously honored at restoration—Infant Ying—yet Guangwu established no precedent of posthumous ancestor designation.

sentences.zh: 設如自我作古，酌於人情，則謂之為「景宣光烈」，深不稱也。

translations.literal: Suppose one follows one's own age and weighs human feeling—then to call him "Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant" is deeply inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Even weighing human sentiment against one's own age, "Illustrious, Propagating, Radiant" is deeply inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 古之周景、漢景、周宣、漢宣，皆中興再造之主。

translations.literal: In antiquity Zhou's Jing, Han's Jing, Zhou's Xuan, and Han's Xuan were all lords who restored the dynasty at its nadir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Jing, Han's Jing, Zhou's Xuan, and Han's Xuan were all rulers who restored the dynasty at its nadir.

sentences.zh: 至如國朝，太祖曰景皇帝，以受命而有唐室，宣宗皇帝以隔代承運，皇綱復振故也。

translations.literal: As for this dynasty, the Grand Ancestor is called Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and possessed the Tang house; Emperor Xuan because across generations he received the fortune and the imperial norm was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In this dynasty the Grand Ancestor is Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and held the Tang house; Emperor Xuan because across generations he received fortune and restored the imperial norm.

sentences.zh: 今輝王亡國墜業，謂之「宣景」，得無謬乎！

translations.literal: Now Emperor Hui lost the state and ruined the enterprise—calling him "Propagating Jing"—is this not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui lost the state and ruined the enterprise—calling him "Propagating Jing"—is this not absurd!

sentences.zh: 先是，太常既奏，下尚書省集議，雖有智者，依違不言。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Court of Imperial Rites had memorialized and the Department of State Affairs convened deliberation, though there were wise men, they wavered and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Rites had memorialized and the Department of State Affairs convened deliberation, wise men wavered and held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 至是，既立為景宗，陵號溫陵，乃於曹州置廟，以時告享，仍以本州刺史以下為三獻官。

translations.literal: At this point, having established him as Emperor Jing, the tomb was named Tomb of Warmth; a temple was set up in Cao Prefecture for seasonal announcement and offering; the prefect of that prefecture and below served as the three presenters.
translations.idiomatic: He was established as Emperor Jing; his tomb was named Tomb of Warmth; a temple was set up in Cao Prefecture for seasonal offerings, with the prefect and subordinates serving as the three presenters.

sentences.zh: 後宰臣知其非，奏去廟號。

translations.literal: Later the chief ministers, knowing this was wrong, memorialized to remove the temple name.
translations.idiomatic: Later chief ministers, recognizing the error, memorialized to remove the temple name.

sentences.zh: 晉天福四年十一月，太常禮院奏：議立唐朝帝廟，引武德年故事，祀隋三帝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: deliberating establishment of Tang imperial temples, citing the Wude-era precedent of sacrificing to the three Sui emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, the Court of Imperial Rites submitted a memorial deliberating Tang imperial temples, citing the Wude-era precedent of sacrificing to the three Sui emperors.

sentences.zh: 今請立近朝莊宗、明宗、閔帝三廟，庶合前規。

translations.literal: We now request establishing temples to the recent rulers Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min, which would accord with former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: We now request temples to the recent rulers Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min, in accord with former regulations.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「德莫盛於繼絕，禮莫重於奉先。

translations.literal: Edict: "No virtue is greater than continuing a severed line; no rite is weightier than honoring ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Edict: "No virtue is greater than continuing a severed line; no rite is weightier than honoring ancestors.

sentences.zh: 莊宗立興復之功，明宗垂光大之業，逮乎閔帝，實繼本枝，然則丕緒洪源，皆尊唐室。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong established the merit of restoration; Mingzong handed down the enterprise of glorious expansion; reaching Emperor Min, he truly continued the main branch—thus the great line and mighty source all honor the Tang house.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong established the merit of restoration; Mingzong handed down glorious expansion; Emperor Min truly continued the main branch—the great line and mighty source all honor the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 繼周者須崇後稷，嗣漢者必奉高皇，將啟嚴祠，當崇茂典。

translations.literal: He who continues Zhou must honor Hou Ji; he who succeeds Han must honor the High Ancestor; about to open solemn sacrifice, the flourishing canon should be honored.
translations.idiomatic: He who continues Zhou must honor Hou Ji; he who succeeds Han must honor the High Ancestor; as solemn sacrifice is about to open, the flourishing canon should be honored.

sentences.zh: 宜立唐高祖、太宗及莊宗、明宗、閔帝五廟。

translations.literal: Tang temples to the High Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min—five temples—should be established.
translations.idiomatic: Tang temples to the High Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min—five temples—should be established.

sentences.zh: 」其月，太常禮院又奏：「唐廟制度，請以至德宮正殿隔為五室，三分之，南去地四尺，以石為坷，中容二主。

translations.literal: " That month the Court of Imperial Rites again memorialized: "For the Tang temple regulations, we request partitioning the main hall of the Palace of Supreme Virtue into five chambers, each one-third in width, four chi from the ground to the south, with stone enclosures in the center holding two spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Court of Imperial Rites again reported: "For Tang temple regulations, partition the main hall of the Palace of Supreme Virtue into five chambers, each one-third in width, four chi from the ground on the south, with stone enclosures holding two spirit tablets each.

sentences.zh: 廟之南一屋三門，門戟二十有四；

translations.literal: South of the temple, one building with three gates, twenty-four halberds at the gates;
translations.idiomatic: South of the temple, one building with three gates and twenty-four halberds;

sentences.zh: 東西一屋一門，門無棨戟。

translations.literal: east and west one building each with one gate, gates without ceremonial halberds.
translations.idiomatic: east and west one building each with one gate, without ceremonial halberds.

sentences.zh: 四仲之祭，一羊一豕，如其中祠，幣帛牲牢之類，光祿主之。

translations.literal: At the four seasonal sacrifices, one sheep and one pig, as for a medium sacrifice; silks, victims, and the like are overseen by the Director of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the four seasonal sacrifices, one sheep and one pig as for a medium sacrifice; silks, victims, and the like are overseen by the Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 祠祝之文，不進不署，神廚之具，鴻臚督之。

translations.literal: Prayer texts are neither advanced nor signed; spirit kitchen implements are supervised by the Court of Honglu.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer texts are neither advanced nor signed; spirit kitchen implements are supervised by the Court of Honglu.

sentences.zh: 五帝五後，凡十主，未遷者六，未立者四，未謚者三。

translations.literal: Five emperors and five empresses—ten lords in all: six not yet removed, four not yet established, three not yet given posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Five emperors and five empresses—ten lords in all: six not yet removed, four not yet established, three not yet given posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太宗與其後暨莊宗、明宗，凡六主在清化裏之寢宮，祭前二日，以殿中傘扇二十，迎置新廟以享祀。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor, and their consorts together with Zhuangzong and Mingzong—six lords in all in the sleeping palace at Qinghua Lane; two days before sacrifice, twenty palace umbrellas and fans are sent to escort them to the new temple for offering.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor, the Grand Ancestor, their consorts, Zhuangzong, and Mingzong—six lords in the sleeping palace at Qinghua Lane; two days before sacrifice, twenty palace umbrellas and fans escort them to the new temple.

sentences.zh: 閔皇帝、莊宗明宗二後及魯國孔夫人神主四座，請修制祔廟，及三後請定謚法。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets of Emperor Min, the two consorts of Zhuangzong and Mingzong, and Lady Kong of Lu—four tablets in all—we request regulations for enshrinement; for the three consorts we request fixing the method of posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets of Emperor Min, the two consorts of Zhuangzong and Mingzong, and Lady Kong of Lu—four tablets—we request enshrinement regulations; for the three consorts we request fixing posthumous title procedure.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.
